excerpt_i18n.en: Today's AI is already impressive. It can write articles, generate code, and create images in seconds, as well as break down tasks, call tools, and provide solutions like an assistant. For many, the future of AI seems clear: higher efficiency, lower costs, less human labor, and increasingly automated production processes. However, Hua Xiansheng, Dean of the Institute of Engineering Intelligence at Tongji University, sees a different side. In his view, the real challenge for AI is not whether it can "speak like a human," but whether it can enter real systems that cannot be solved by language fluency alone. The engineering world is such a system—it concerns whether buildings are safe, bridges are reliable, traffic is smooth, energy can be stably dispatched, and cities can operate continuously. There are no simple standard answers here, nor can hallucinations be passed off as creativity. Even if an AI model can produce a perfect plan, it does not mean it understands the engineering site. Therefore, the first question engineering intelligence must answer is: How can AI move from the digital world to the physical world? Dean Hua believes that engineering intelligence is not a simple combination of AI and engineering. It must not only use existing AI technologies to solve engineering problems but also derive new AI theories and methods from complex engineering systems. Moreover, these capabilities must be solidified into platforms, models, intelligent agents, and operating systems, enabling engineering intelligence to scale from single-point breakthroughs to widespread replication. This is the judgment he has formed after moving from Microsoft and Alibaba's City Brain to the Institute of Engineering Intelligence at Tongji University: AI implementation cannot rely solely on "holding a hammer to find
excerpt_i18n.es: La IA actual ya es lo suficientemente impresionante. Para muchos, el futuro de la IA parece ya claro: mayor eficiencia, menores costos, menos mano de obra y procesos de producción cada vez más automatizados. excerpt_i18n.en:
On May 19, in Beijing, ZhiXiang Future held its first Open Day themed "Imaging the World." During the event, the company officially launched HiDream-O1-Image-Pro, an image large model built on the next-generation native full-modal architecture Unified Transformer (UiT). This native full-modal image large model, with over 200 billion parameters, not only sets new SOTA records across multiple benchmarks but also marks ZhiXiang Future's advancement toward unified modeling of images, videos, text, audio, and other modalities in the "native full-modal" stage.  

Meanwhile, ZhiXiang Future announced the completion of a new round of financing worth hundreds of millions of yuan, with participation from institutions including Shenzhen Capital Group, Jinpu Investment, Caixin Capital, and Fuju Capital. This marks another financing round for ZhiXiang Future within half a month, reflecting the capital market's continued optimism for the native full-modal large model direction. As frontier technologies such as visual generation and embodied intelligence accelerate their integration, world models have become a key direction for AI evolution. ZhiXiang Future's sustained breakthroughs in underlying model architecture, productization capabilities, and industrial ecosystem layout have further gained market recognition.  

The 200B+ parameter image large model HiDream-O1-Image-Pro has been released, with a comprehensive upgrade of the native full-modal architecture.  

Currently, image generation models are transitioning from the traditional U-Net architecture to diffusion Transformer (DiT).
excerpt_i18n.es: El 19 de mayo, en Pekín. Zhixiang Future celebró su primera jornada de puertas abiertas bajo el lema "Imaging the World". Durante el evento, Zhixiang Future lanzó oficialmente el gran modelo de imagen HiDream-O1-Image-Pro, basado en la nueva arquitectura de modelo nativo totalmente multimodal Unified Transformer (UiT). Este gran modelo de imagen nativo totalmente multimodal, con más de 200 mil millones de parámetros, no solo ha establecido nuevos récords SOTA en múltiples pruebas de referencia, sino que también marca el avance de Zhixiang Future hacia la etapa de "modelo nativo totalmente multimodal", que unifica modelado de imagen, video, texto, audio y otras modalidades.

excerpt_i18n.en: On May 20, the 2026 "ByteDance Scholarship" officially opened for applications. The scholarship targets university students in cutting-edge technology fields, offering a cash reward of up to 300,000 RMB per awardee and their advisor. This year, the program has expanded its application scope to universities worldwide for the first time, and the number of awardees will exceed last year's 20 recipients. Additionally, the program pioneered a 100,000 RMB advisor bonus in the industry to recognize advisors' contributions to talent cultivation. Beyond financial support, the ByteDance Scholarship also focuses on broadening the academic horizons of young scholars. Awardees will be invited to join the ByteScholars research community, engaging in regular exchanges with renowned scholars, industry experts, and past recipients. excerpt_i18n.en: In recent years, the lifelines of U.S. AI giants have seemed tightly held by Nvidia, until Cerebras stepped into the spotlight with its $67 billion market cap. Last night Beijing time, an American company selling "big chips"—Cerebras—made a stellar debut on Nasdaq: its closing price surged 68% above the IPO price, reaching a total market value of $67 billion. "This is the largest IPO so far this year and also sets a record for the listing of a 'pure AI chip company' in U.S. stock market history," said Zhang Lin, an analyst who has long tracked U.S. hardware stocks, to Leiphone. On the surface, this is a high-tech wealth-creating IPO; but in the eyes of Silicon Valley's core circle, it feels more like the starting gun for an impending "computing power reshuffle." "Cerebras's listing means that non-GPU paths can not only survive but also command astonishing premiums," Zhang Lin noted. The chip industry has begun to move away from the single-choice era of "buying cards and paying taxes," with differentiated architectures truly emerging. Moreover, according to computing power industry investor Wang Ning, this IPO is also, to some extent, shifting the power landscape of the U.S. AI camp. Behind Cerebras stand giants eager to redefine the power hierarchy of the AI era. "This is not just a simple listing, but a 'chip catfish' officially entering the game, triggering a 'critical moment' in the global AI industry's discourse power struggle," Wang Ning emphasized. For more intriguing insights, feel free to add the author's WeChat.
excerpt_i18n.es: En los últimos años, el destino de los gigantes tecnológicos de IA en EE. UU. parecía estar en manos de Nvidia, hasta que Cerebras apareció en el foco con una valoración de 67 000 millones de dólares. Ayer, hora de Pekín, una empresa estadounidense que vende "chips grandes", Cerebras, debutó en el Nasdaq con un rendimiento excepcional: su precio de cierre subió un 68 % respecto al precio de emisión, alcanzando una capitalización de mercado total de 67 000 millones de dólares. "Esta es la OPI más grande del año hasta la fecha y también establece un récord en la historia del mercado de valores de EE. UU. para la cotización de una 'empresa pura de chips de IA'", comentó Zhang Lin, analista que sigue de cerca los activos de hardware en el mercado estadounidense, a Leiphone. En apariencia, se trata de una OPI que genera riqueza a través de la alta tecnología.

Academically, Dr. Liu served as the area chair for the top robotics conference CoRL 20/21 and as a reviewer for Nature sub-journals, publishing over 80 papers in top AI journals and conferences. Co-founder and CTO Tao Shuai also graduated from the Department of Electronic Engineering at Tsinghua University and previously led search and affiliate network business at ByteDance.
